To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the epigenetic regulation of the TNFA gene in periodontal tissue is a complex process involving DNA methylation, histone modification, and noncoding RNA.
1) the epigenetic mechanism of TNFA regulation is different in periodontal and rheumatoid disease and 2) TNFA expression in the gingiva is regulated by DNA methylation and histone modifications.
the expression of TNF-α in periodontal tissue was regulated by epigenetic mechanisms, and that this epigenetic regulation may be associated with the pathogenesis of periodontal disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of epigenetic regulation of gene expression in periodontitis.
understanding the molecular basis for the regulation of the TNFα gene in the context of periodontal disease and with the development of a new class of anti-inflammatory drugs.
the role of TNFA in periodontal diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epigenetic regulation of gene expression is a complex process that is influenced by a multitude of factors.
the epigenetic modifications of the TNFA gene are associated with the development and progression of periodontal diseases.

the epigenetic modifications in the promoter region of the TNFA gene, as shown in this study, may contribute to its overexpression, which in turn is associated with chronic inflammation and tissue destruction in the periodontium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the first epigenetic regulator of TNFA in periodontal diseases.

we have identified a novel epigenetic mechanism for TNFA regulation in periodontal tissue and that this epigenetic mechanism can be targeted to prevent the progression of periodontal tissue destruction.
the epigenome is a dynamic entity, and the dynamic nature of the epigenome can be exploited for therapeutic purposes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a new class of small molecules that have the ability to target the epigenetic machinery of cells and that these molecules can be used to modulate the activity of the NFκB pathway.
epigenetics can be an effective tool to study the role of environmental factors in complex disease.
we can use the information in our epigenomes to predict how cells will respond to environmental cues.
